To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated crystallographically oriented n type Bi2Se3 xTe x nanomaterial with high ZT values, which were produced from asymmetric colloidal nanocrystal (NC) precursors.
we demonstrate crystallographic texturing and enhanced thermoelectric properties in Bi2Te3Se3 by consolidating asymmetric disk shaped Bi2 Te3 xSe x NCs with a high excess of tellurie.
we demonstrate crystallographic texture in n type Bi2SeTe nanomaterials by hot pressing disk shaped nanocrystals in the presence of excess tellurium.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and understanding of new thermoelectric nanomaterials and their processing.

the development and characterization of crystallographically textural n type Bi2T e3 xSe x thermoelectric nanomaterials produced by hot pressing disk-shaped Bi2Te3x Se x colloidal nanocrytals in the presence of excess tellurium, which resulted in very high electrical conductivites, low thermal conductivities and high ZT values.
the development of high thermoelectric performance n type Bi2SeTe alloys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of colloidal nanocrystal building blocks, combined with crystallographic texture and an excess of tellerium during hot pressing, resulted in the highest thermoelectric figures ever reported in the Bi2Te3 based system.
crystallographic texture, in conjunction with the presence of an extra Te source, can be used to achieve very high thermoelectric performance in Bi2Te3 based materials.

the use of disk shaped colloidal nanocrystal precursors and the presence of tellurium both as lubricant and solvent, resulted in a very effective consolidation of n type Bi2 Te3 xSe x with a crystallographic texture that is beneficial for thermoelectric performance.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

crystallographic texturing of Bi2Te3Se2 nanomaterials, achieved by hot pressing asymmetric disk shaped colloidal nanocrystal, results in a ca. 30% increase in the electrical conductivity and a ca. 60% reduction of the thermal conductivity in the pressing direction.
crystallographically oriented Bi2Te3Se nanomaterials, produced by hot pressing asymmetric NCs, show high electrical conductivities and low thermal conductivities along the pressing direction.
the combination of crystallographic texture with the presence of TeBi antisite and Te spillover donors in between grains led to high thermoelectric performance.
The main takeaway from our work is that
crystallographic texture is an important parameter to consider in the development of high ZT materials, especially when the thermoelectric properties are anisotropic.

the use of asymmetric NCs with different aspect ratios in different directions allows for the production of textured nanomaterials that can be hot pressed to form bulk materials with very high thermoelectric figures.
the thermoelectric properties of Bi2Te3 can be significantly improved by the combination of two factors, i.e., crystallographic texture and the presence of an additional phase.
